verdict: Salesforce grew revenue 8% to $9.44B and — by holding cost growth below sales growth — turned it into $1.53B of profit, up 25% from a year ago, in the quarter it launched Agentforce, its AI-agent platform.

segments.name: Subscription and support
segments.note: Renting Salesforce's software — sales, service, marketing, Slack, Tableau and the rest — plus support. The recurring base of the business: 94 cents of every revenue dollar.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Consultants who help customers set the software up — a people-heavy business Salesforce is deliberately keeping small.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform — including Agentforce, Salesforce's AI agents, launched this quarter — up 13% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The largest running cost — Salesforce's big sales force and marketing machine, up 5% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — up 12% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring
opex.note: One-off costs of reorganizing teams and facilities.

otherDetail: A $217M loss on Salesforce's strategic investments — paper markdowns on stakes it holds in other companies — partly offset by $70M of other income: a net $147M cost.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Margin discipline is the story
takeaways.text: Operating margin reached 20%, up from 17% a year ago: Salesforce grew revenue 8% while its costs grew more slowly. Profit rose 25% even though a $217M paper loss on strategic investments sat below the operating line.

takeaways.title: Subscriptions did the growing
takeaways.text: Subscription and support revenue rose 9% to $8.88B — 94 cents of every dollar — while professional services shrank slightly. This was also the launch quarter for Agentforce, Salesforce's AI agents and its biggest product bet of the year.

takeaways.title: Restructuring is now a habit
takeaways.text: Salesforce booked another $56M restructuring charge — its third straight year of periodic reorganization costs. Small next to $9.4B of revenue, but a recurring feature of how the company now manages its cost base.

oneTimers: A $217M loss on strategic investments — unrealized markdowns on stakes Salesforce holds in other tech companies.
A $56M restructuring charge inside operating expenses.
